source: Our simulations are the first of their kind to capture repeatedly Myr insertion through unbiased all-atom MD simulations.
evidence: This claims a novel achievement of the study.

claim: The time scale for insertion is on average 50 ns.
source: Through our analysis, we show the time scale for insertion is on average 50 ns
evidence: This is a quantitative finding about the insertion timescale.

claim: As Myr unrolls into the binding leaflet, the first helix in the protein sequence, H1, shifts to rest flat on the membrane surface.
source: As Myr unrolls into the binding leaflet, the first helix in the protein sequence, H1, shifts to rest flat on the membrane surface.
evidence: This describes conformational changes during Myr insertion.

claim: The first and last carbons in the Myr tail, C2 and C14 respectively, pass each other as the tail inserts into the leaflet.
source: The first and last carbons in the Myr tail, C2 and C14 respectively, pass each other as the tail inserts into the leaflet.
evidence: This describes the detailed mechanism of Myr insertion.

claim: Depending on the location of Myr prior to insertion, C14 can extend vertically toward the solvent or enter the leaflet 'sweeping' the membrane surface as Myr unrolls into the leaflet from a flat position between the protein and the membrane.
source: Depending on the location of Myr prior to insertion, C14 can extend vertically toward the solvent or enter the leaflet 'sweeping' the membrane surface as Myr unrolls into the leaflet from a flat position between the protein and the membrane.
evidence: This describes variability in the insertion mechanism depending on initial Myr position.

claim: tICA identified the HBR, H1, and H5 as key protein regions that modulate or contribute to the insertion process.
source: This mechanism was further characterized using tICA, identifying the HBR, H1, and H5 as key protein regions that modulate or contribute to the insertion process.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the tICA analysis.

claim: Myr only inserts into the inner membrane model, that mimics the inner leaflet of the PM in terms of anionic lipids, lipid tail unsaturation, and sterol content.
source: Importantly, we built three membrane models to study the effect of different membrane mechanical and structural properties on insertion events. We found Myr only inserts into our inner membrane model, that mimics the inner leaflet of the PM in terms of anionic lipids, lipid tail unsaturation, and sterol content.
evidence: This is a key finding about membrane specificity of Myr insertion.

claim: A combination of membrane surface charge, lipid packing, and the degree of lipid tail unsaturation inside the bilayer are key determinants for Myr insertion.
source: From these studies, we conclude that a combination of membrane surface charge, lipid packing, and the degree of lipid tail unsaturation inside the bilayer are key determinants for Myr insertion.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the factors determining Myr insertion.

claim: The surface charge for the inner and control models are similar.
source: From Table 1, the surface charge for the inner and control models are similar
evidence: This is a comparison of membrane properties, with reference to a table.

claim: The presence of sterol in the inner model results in an overall more saturated and ordered environment that Myr prefers.
source: yet the presence of sterol in the inner model results in an overall more saturated and ordered environment that Myr prefers.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the role of sterols in creating a favorable environment for Myr insertion.

claim: One expects more defects on the surface of the control model due to its lack of cholesterol and more fluid nature.
source: Packing defects on the membrane surface also play a role; one expects more defects on the surface of the control model due to its lack of cholesterol and more fluid nature
evidence: This is an inference about membrane properties based on composition.

claim: The unsaturation degree and disorder of the control membrane hydrophobic core do not seem to provide an optimum or attractive place for Myr.
source: but the unsaturation degree and disorder of the membrane hydrophobic core do not seem to provide an optimum or attractive place for Myr.
evidence: This is a conclusion about why Myr doesn't insert into the control model despite having defects.

claim: The raft model with high sterol and sphingomyelin content seems too tightly packed and ordered for any insertion event to occur, even with multiple MA units.
source: Finally, the raft model with high sterol and sphingomyelin content seems too tightly packed and ordered for any insertion event to occur, even with multiple MA units.
evidence: This is a conclusion about why Myr doesn't insert into the raft model.

claim: The protein was randomly positioned near the membrane surface after a short equilibration in solvent, so the effect of lipid domains on initial protein binding or Myr insertion has not been quantified.
source: The protein was randomly positioned near the membrane surface after a short equilibration in solvent, so we have not quantified the effect of lipid domains on initial protein binding or Myr insertion.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the study design.

claim: Insertion of Myr results in modifications of lipid order as quantified by the order parameter SCD.
source: We have shown, however, that insertion of Myr results in modifications of lipid order as quantified by the order parameter SCD.
evidence: This is a finding about the effect of Myr insertion on membrane properties.

claim: The effect of a single monomer on lipid order is not as dramatic, altering the order of the last carbons in the long sphingomyelin lipid tails.
source: The effect is not as dramatic for the case of a single monomer, which alters the order of the last carbons in the long sphingomyelin lipid tails.
evidence: This describes the limited effect of a single MA unit on lipid order.

claim: The presence of a formed trimer that enables quicker Myr insertion induces increase in order in the mid-region of sphingomyelin lipids.
source: However, the presence of a formed trimer that enables quicker Myr insertion, induces increase in order in the mid-region of the same lipids.
evidence: This describes the enhanced effect of multiple MA units on lipid order.

claim: Results present evidence that an increasing number of protein units enhances the changes observed on the membrane upon MA binding.
source: Our results present evidence that an increasing number of protein units enhances the changes observed on the membrane upon MA binding, as would be the case at early stages of the viral assembly process of HIV-1 in the cell.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the cumulative effect of multiple MA units.

claim: Protein-lipid interactions recruit specific lipid species, like PIP2, to the protein binding site changing the local lipid composition.
source: Particularly, protein-lipid interactions recruit specific lipid species, like PIP2, to the protein binding site changing the local lipid composition.
evidence: This describes the effect of MA binding on local lipid distribution.

claim: Changes in local lipid composition can influence the recruitment of other crucial components for the virus, creating a more suitable platform to continue and complete viral assembly and posterior budding.
source: In turn, this also changes the local membrane properties and can influence the recruitment of other crucial components for the virus, creating a more suitable platform to continue and complete viral assembly and posterior budding.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the biological significance of the observed lipid recruitment.

claim: Symmetric membrane models were examined in this study, and a study with asymmetric models is reserved for a separate publication.
source: One of the main characteristics of the PM is the asymmetry between its bilayers; here, we examined symmetric membrane models and reserved a study with asymmetric models for a separate publication.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation and describes future work.

claim: The MA domain is a conserved domain of Gag across several retroviruses.
source: The MA domain is a conserved domain of Gag across several retroviruses, thus we expect our conclusions to also provide insight into the mechanism of binding in other viral systems (Mattei et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement about the conservation of MA, supported by a citation.

claim: The conclusions are expected to provide insight into the mechanism of binding in other viral systems.
source: The MA domain is a conserved domain of Gag across several retroviruses, thus we expect our conclusions to also provide insight into the mechanism of binding in other viral systems (Mattei et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculation about the broader applicability of the findings.

claim: Fundamental understanding of the membrane targeting mechanism of MA can offer new perspectives for inhibitor-based antiretroviral treatments.
source: Fundamental understanding of the membrane targeting mechanism of MA can offer new perspectives for inhibitor-based antiretroviral treatments (Zentner et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about potential applications, supported by a citation.

claim: This work contributes to the study of lipidated peripheral proteins and their interactions with membranes in the context of macromolecular assembly.
source: This work contributes to the study of lipidated peripheral proteins and their interactions with membranes in the context of macromolecular assembly.
evidence: This is a statement about the broader significance of the work.
